properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: @noble/curves@1.9.7 provides the secp256k1 module the BTC/ETH flows use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring@0.17.14 (Rust, via Cargo.lock — most likely pulled by rustls for canister outbound TLS) and the npm tree both ship Ed25519. Available in the shipped libraries; the production Ed25519 use in this repo is ICP t-schnorr (schnorr_public_key for the Solana path in service.rs) and the signer's schnorr.ed25519 master pubkey — keys are held threshold-style by the ICP network: observable here, replaceable only by the platform.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: No P-256 call site found in application code (the app uses secp256k1 and Ed25519); the library ships P-256 ECDSA/ECDH in its API surface regardless — presence is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring@0.17.14 is the Rust crypto provider pulled in (likely via rustls) for the backend canister; its X25519 agreement is available in the shipped binary whether or not the app calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 5 sites execute real WebCrypto HKDF (subtle.importKey('raw', …, 'HKDF') + deriveKey) inside the vetKeys test suites for personal-notes and tips — reproducing the client-side key derivation the @dfinity/vetkeys dependency performs in production (X25519 transport ECDH → HKDF → AES-GCM key). Executed cryptography, test-only scope; the production derivation lives inside the @dfinity/vetkeys wrapper, whose call sites are in personal-notes.vetkeys.ts / tip.vetkeys.ts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: model.rs:27 is the live production site: HMAC-SHA256 (RustCrypto hmac+sha2) over the canonicalized Onramper widget-URL parameters with a controller-provided secret, hex-encoded as the signature query param. The three wallet-connect spec sites wire @noble/hashes hmac(sha256) into @noble/secp256k1's etc.hmacSha256Sync — required because only tests sign there (production only recovers public keys, which needs no HMAC); real HMAC-SHA256 execution on the test-only signing path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: personal-note-share.crypto.ts:27 is the live production site: WebCrypto AES-GCM-256 (KEY_LENGTH_BITS = 256 — the object's AES-128 floor grade is pessimistic), fresh random 96-bit IV per encryption prepended to the ciphertext, share token bound as AAD (<token>:note), per-share key generated in-browser and transported only in the URL fragment. Lockfile sites: the Rust aes-gcm crate and npm packages that provide AES-GCM in the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 crate is live in the backend (HMAC-SHA256 for Onramper URL signing in onramper/model.rs, tips model, account conversion); the npm side provides SHA-256 to bitcoinjs-lib/@noble (BTC hash256 digests). The build ships SHA-256 in both toolchains.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto hmac crate — live production use at src/backend/src/onramper/model.rs:27, HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized Onramper widget-URL parameters with a controller-provided secret, surfaced as the signature query parameter.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 module available in the shipped @noble/hashes@1.8.0 bundle; no direct application call site found. Presence is the inventory question — the image ships the algorithm in its frontend bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 module surface available to the frontend; Keccak-256 hashing in the Rust signer is served by tiny-keccak (ALG-052c24b2).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production WebCrypto SHA-512 in deriveXrpTransactionHash: computes the XRP Ledger transaction ID (SHA-512Half — first 256 bits of SHA-512(0x54584E00 ‖ signed blob)) so the UI can poll for inclusion without trusting the submit response. Protocol-mandated digest format on the live send path; quantum-safe (symmetric), no migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 ships ChaCha20-Poly1305 alongside its AES modules; the app's envelope encryption uses AES-GCM via WebCrypto; ChaCha20-Poly1305 recorded as available library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes ships in the frontend bundle: direct imports in the BTC test suite (hmac + sha256 wired into @noble/secp256k1's etc.hmacSha256Sync) and transitively under bitcoinjs-lib (sha256/sha512/ripemd160 for BIP32 derivation and script hashes) and @dfinity libraries. API surface on disk: sha2, hmac, ripemd160, blake3, keccak, etc.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.9.7 is the project's elliptic-curve library: its secp256k1 module powers the BTC/ETH address/signature flows (ALG-673c8f24) and Ed25519 the ICP/SOL/Near flows (ALG-5e08bdf5); its P-256 module ships unused (ALG-a6da3577). Version 1.9.7 is the one that decides available curves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RustCrypto sha2 crate — directly used across the backend: onramper/model.rs (HMAC-SHA256 widget-URL signing), tips/model.rs, backend tests, shared account conversion. Live dependency, not merely declared.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The app's own code imports @noble/secp256k1 (btc/utils/wallet-connect.utils.ts:14) and tests import @noble/hashes + @noble/secp256k1; no @noble/ciphers import found anywhere — recorded as shipped library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.23.43 offers TLS 1.3 with classical ECDHE key exchange only (X25519/secp256r1/P-384 — no PQ groups); observable here, but the canister never opens TLS — the IC boundary nodes (DFINITY) terminate HTTPS, and the production wasm does not embed this stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 enters the backend build (most likely via rustls, which the backend uses for outbound HTTPS from canisters). Ships Ed25519, ECDSA P-256, X25519, AES-GCM, SHA-2 in the shipped library; the application's primary signature crypto (t-ECDSA/t-schnorr) lives on the ICP platform side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The same lockfile entry is carried as an AES-GCM algorithm sighting under ALG-f61ec50f (personal-note-share.crypto.ts:27, Cargo.lock) — this entry is the provider facet: the Rust crate ic-vetkeys pulls in for its encrypted-map values.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The provisioned OnRamper signing secret (SEC-ce809021) is the key that feeds this HMAC; verification of the widget URL happens in the frontend.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same lockfile entry as the TLS 1.3 object (ALG-f42564d9): one stack, two facets — rustls (provider) and TLS 1.3 (protocol capability).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure: provisions the OnRamper widget-URL signing secret (used by sign_onramper_widget_url / the HMAC-SHA-256 in src/backend/src/onramper/model.rs) into backend canister state; secret sourced from --secret flag / ONRAMPER_SIGNING_SECRET env / non-echoed prompt, inherited $SECRET deliberately unset — no hardcoded material.
